B1_EXC.name: B1_EXC
B1_EXC.description:
Excessive errors on the regenerator section (B1). This alarm is generated when the received SDH signals 
degrade and the B1 bit errors on the regenerator section exceed the threshold.
B1_EXC.impact:
The B1 bit errors in the service signals received by a board exceed the B1 bit error threshold set for the 
board. The alarm affects the QoS of the service signals.
B1_EXC.fault_symptom:
None.
 
If the fault has no symptom, or if the fault symptom is not covered in this topic, handle the fault according to 
"Handling Procedure" provided in this topic.
possible_causes: (reported from the client side): The input signals on the client side contain B1 bit errors.
(reported from the client side): The board that reports this alarm is faulty.
(reported from the WDM side): The receive side of the local station (Station B) is faulty. ===== PAGE 179 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 177
(reported from the WDM side): The attenuation of the received signals is excessively high; the fiber or connector is not clean.
(reported from the WDM side): The transmit side of the opposite station (Station A) is faulty.

BD_STATUS.name: BD_STATUS
BD_STATUS.description:
===== PAGE 181 =====
Physical board being offline. This alarm is generated when the logical board is created on the NCE but the 
physical board is not inserted in the slot.
BD_STATUS.impact: The board is offline. Therefore, the functions related to the board are unavailable.
possible_causes: The logical board is configured but the physical board has not been inserted in the corresponding slot.
The connection between the plug of the board and the socket of the backplane is loose.
The board is faulty.
If multiple boards report this alarm, the EFI board may be faulty.
The backplane is faulty.

BEFFEC_EXC.name: BEFFEC_EXC
BEFFEC_EXC.description:
Signal degraded before FEC. Signals sent from the WDM side of the opposite-end OTU have the FEC 
function. As a result, before performing signal FEC in the receive direction on the WDM side of the local-
end OTU, the local-end OTU counts the bit error rate. This alarm is generated when the counted bit error 
rate crosses the threshold.
BEFFEC_EXC.impact: The error tolerance of the system decreases, which may even affect the quality of signals.
BEFFEC_EXC.fault_symptom:

An inappropriate DCM is installed.

BIOS_STATUS.name: BIOS_STATUS
BIOS_STATUS.description:
===== PAGE 186 =====
The BIOS_STATUS is an alarm indicating the BIOS status. By default, if loading of the board software fails 
for three consecutive times within five minutes, the board enters the BIOS status and the BIOS_STATUS 
alarm is reported.
BIOS_STATUS.impact:
When an abnormality occurs on the board software or hardware, the BIOS_STATUS alarm is generated and 
related services are interrupted.
possible_causes: The software is lost.
Incorrect software is loaded.
Writing or reading the software becomes abnormal.
The board hardware is faulty.
The board software is not synchronized.

BOOTROM_BAD.name: BOOTROM_BAD
BOOTROM_BAD.description:
A BOOTROM data check fails. This alarm is reported when the basic or extended BIOS software of the 
system control board is damaged.
BOOTROM_BAD.impact:
When powered on again or reset after a power supply failure, the system control board cannot be 
normally started.
possible_causes: The system control board is faulty.
The BOOTROM data area of the board is damaged.

BP_ODU_LOFLOM.name: BP_ODU_LOFLOM
BP_ODU_LOFLOM.description:
BP_ODU_LOFLOM indicates the loss of ODUk frames and multiframes in the backplane direction of an 
OTN line board. This alarm is reported when the frame header information of the source board and sink 
board (the line board that reports the alarm) does not match.
BP_ODU_LOFLOM.impact: The OTN service that traverses this line board is interrupted or has a bit error.
possible_causes: The sink board is faulty.
The source board is faulty.
The cross-connect board is faulty.
The rate modes of corresponding channels on the source and sink boards are inconsistent.

BUS_ERR.name: BUS_ERR
BUS_ERR.description: Backplane bus error. This alarm is generated when the board detects a backplane bus error.
BUS_ERR.impact:
• This alarm triggers the bus switching.
• Services are unavailable or bit errors are generated.
BUS_ERR.fault_symptom:
None
 
If the fault has no symptom, or if the fault symptom is not covered in this topic, handle the fault according to 
"Handling Procedure" provided in this topic.
===== PAGE 194 =====
2026-04-22 192
possible_causes: The OTU, tributary, or line board is not properly inserted or is faulty.
The cross-connect board is not properly inserted or is faulty.
The type of services that are actually received does not match the service type configured on the board.
The pins are faulty or the bus is faulty on the backplane.
The logical board of the cross-connect board is not created.
The frequency deviation of input signals on the tributary board is excessively large.
When this alarm is reported by a cluster cross-connect board, the optical port on the cross- connect board is faulty.
When the cross-connect board reported the alarm, the service board was faulty.

CHAN_LOS.name: CHAN_LOS
CHAN_LOS.description:
===== PAGE 196 =====
Single-wavelength signal loss or performance (the center wavelength, power, or OSNR) degrade alarm. 
The alarm is generated when the multi-channel spectrum analyzer (MCA) board detects that the original 
wavelength is lost or the optical spectrum performance degrade amount exceeds the threshold after it 
scans the optical spectrum.
CHAN_LOS.impact:
• The services of the related wavelength are unavailable.
• The MCA cannot monitor the optical spectrum performance of the wavelength related to the alarm.
CHAN_LOS.fault_symptom:
None.
 
If the fault has no symptom, or if the fault symptom is not covered in this topic, handle the fault according to 
"Handling Procedure" provided in this topic.
possible_causes: The wavelength that needs to be monitored is not received or the shift of the monitored wavelength exceeds 0.15 nm. For example, in the following figure, λ1 needs to be monitored as ===== PAGE 197 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 195 configured, but actually λ1 is not received.
The laser on the board at the opposite station is turned off. For example, the laser on OTU1 in the preceding figure is turned off.
The optical power difference between the monitored wavelengths is excessively large. For example, the optical power difference between λ1 and λ2 is excessively large.
The attenuation of the multiplexer or OA board interconnected with the MCA is excessively high.
The OTU board located before the MCA is faulty. For example, OTU1 in the preceding figure is faulty.
The MCA that reports the alarm is faulty.

CLIENT_PORT_PS.name: CLIENT_PORT_PS
CLIENT_PORT_PS.description:
Client-side 1+1 protection switching. This alarm is generated when a client 1+1 protection group 
undergoes protection switching and the active channel is switched from the working channel to the 
protection channel.
CLIENT_PORT_PS.impact:
When a client 1+1 protection group undergoes protection switching, services are transiently interrupted. 
When this alarm is generated, the working channel of the client 1+1 protection group might have services 
that needs to be restored.
===== PAGE 200 =====
2026-04-22 198

The services on the working channel of a client 1+1 protection group are faulty and the active channel automatically switches to the working channel, triggering the CLIENT_PORT_PS alarm.

COMMUN_FAIL.name: COMMUN_FAIL
COMMUN_FAIL.description:
Inter-board communication failure. This alarm is generated when the communication between system 
control boards and other boards is interrupted.
COMMUN_FAIL.impact:
Services may fail to be configured, protection switching may fail, or versions may be unexpectedly rolled 
back during package loading. When this occurs, new services will be abnormal.
For OSN 9800 U/M/K series subracks, after one COMMUN_FAIL alarm with the parameter being 0x03 and 
another with the parameter being 0x04 are both generated, configurations cannot be delivered to boards

DBMS_ERROR.name: DBMS_ERROR
DBMS_ERROR.description: Database error. The alarm is generated when the database is in error.
DBMS_ERROR.impact:
• The database cannot be restored automatically.
• The system configuration data may be lost. A failure message may be displayed in response to certain 
query or setting commands. The functions of the system may be unavailable.
• Inconsistent boards or ports exist in the database, causing a failure to execute the board or port 
related operation command.
possible_causes: The database operation fails.
Data in the database is damaged.
The board is faulty.
The configuration file fails to be saved because the storage space is full.
The database status does not support saving.
The saving fails due to a file backup failure.
The saving fails due to other errors.

FAN_FAIL.name: FAN_FAIL
FAN_FAIL.description: Fan failure. This alarm is generated when two or more fans fail.
FAN_FAIL.impact:
The failure of two or more fans leads to the increase in the board temperature and even the damage to 
the board.
possible_causes: The speed of the fans is excessively low.
The fan power supply is abnormal.
The board is in poor contact with the backplane.
The fans stop running. ===== PAGE 211 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 209
The fans fail.

FAN_FAULT.name: FAN_FAULT
FAN_FAULT.description: Fan fault. This alarm is generated when a fan fails.
FAN_FAULT.impact:
The failure of one fan may lead to the increase in the board temperature and even the damage to the 
board.
possible_causes: One fan fails.
The logical inspection fails. ===== PAGE 212 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 210

HARD_BAD.name: HARD_BAD
HARD_BAD.description: Hardware failure. This alarm is generated when the system detects a hardware failure.
HARD_BAD.impact: The alarm affects the normal operating of the board and affects services.
possible_causes: The NE power supplies are abnormal.
The board is not connected to the backplane properly or the board is faulty.
The optical module is faulty.
The slot in the subrack is faulty. ===== PAGE 215 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 213

The device type in the EPPROM of the backplane fails to pass the verification, or the device type in the EPPROM of the backplane is different with that in the logic of the system control board, or the device type of the EPPROM on the backplane is inconsistent with that in the memory of the system co
The PSU is faulty.

HARD_NONSUPPORT.name: HARD_NONSUPPORT
HARD_NONSUPPORT.description:
===== PAGE 221 =====
Not supported by the hardware. This alarm is generated when the board hardware does not support the 
board configuration, or the total power consumption of all inserted boards exceeds the upper limit of the 
device power consumption.
HARD_NONSUPPORT.impact:
When this alarm is reported, the board configuration cannot take effect. Specifically, if this alarm is 
reported during service configuration, the service fails to be applied to the hardware and therefore cannot 
be deployed. If this alarm is reported when IEEE 1588 is enabled, the IEEE 1588 function will fail to be 
enabled.

IN_PWR_HIGH.name: IN_PWR_HIGH
IN_PWR_HIGH.description:
Input optical power being too high. This alarm is generated when the input optical power is higher than 
the upper threshold of the input optical power.
IN_PWR_HIGH.impact:
When the input optical power is excessively high, bit errors and LOF alarms may be generated in the 
received signals, and the optical module on the board can be damaged. As a result, the services are 
affected.
IN_PWR_HIGH.fault_symptom:
None
 
If the fault has no symptom, or if the fault symptom is not covered in this topic, handle the fault according to 
"Handling Procedure" provided in this topic.
possible_causes: (reported from the client side): The input optical power is excessively high, and the attenuation configured is insufficient or the attenuator is faulty.
(reported from the client side): The board that reports this alarm is faulty.
(reported from the WDM side): The output optical power of the board in the upstream station is excessively high.
(reported from the WDM side): The board that reports this alarm is faulty.

IN_PWR_LOW.name: IN_PWR_LOW
IN_PWR_LOW.description:
Input optical power being too low. The alarm is generated when the input optical power is smaller than 
the lower threshold of the input optical power.
IN_PWR_LOW.impact:
If the input optical power is excessively low, bit errors may be generated in the received signals, which 
affect the normal receiving of the services.
possible_causes: (reported from the client side): The fiber connector is dirty, and the fiber jumper is over-bent, damaged or aged.
(reported from the client side): The attenuation of the attenuator attached to the optical port on the board that reports this alarm is excessively high.
(reported from the client side): The board that reports this alarm is faulty.
(reported from the WDM side): The fiber connector is dirty, and the fiber jumper is over-bent, damaged or aged.

(reported from the WDM side): The attenuation of the attenuator attached to the optical port on the board that reports this alarm is excessively high. ===== PAGE 229 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 227
(reported from the WDM side): The attenuation attached to the transmit optical port on the board at the opposite station is excessively high, or the transmit optical module is faulty.
(reported from the WDM side): The attenuation in the transmission of the optical signals is excessively high and the compensation is insufficient.
(reported from the WDM side): The board that reports this alarm is faulty.

INNER_COMMUN_MISCON.name: INNER_COMMUN_MISCON
INNER_COMMUN_MISCON.description:
Incorrect connection between an internal network and an external network. This alarm is generated when 
the device cascading ports are incorrectly connected or the inter-board communication port of the subrack 
slot is disabled or a loop occurs in the inter-board communication of the subrack slot.
INNER_COMMUN_MISCON.impact:
The communication data between the NE and each board is abnormal, and configuration query commands 
cannot be processed normally.
possible_causes: The device cascading ports are incorrectly connected or the inter-board communication port of the subrack slot is disabled or a loop occurs in the inter-board communication of the subrack slot.

INSUFFCNT_FLSH_SPACE.name: INSUFFCNT_FLSH_SPACE
INSUFFCNT_FLSH_SPACE.description: This alarm indicates the space of the flash file system is insufficient.
INSUFFCNT_FLSH_SPACE.impact:
===== PAGE 234 =====
The flash file storage space is insufficient. As a result, file storage in the flash fails.

LAN_LOC.name: LAN_LOC
LAN_LOC.description:
Ethernet communication failure. In the case of NE cascading, this alarm is generated when the Ethernet 
communication between NEs fails.
LAN_LOC.impact:
The communication at this network port fails and some NEs may be unreachable by the NCE, but the 
services on the NEs are not affected.

LASER_MOD_ERR.name: LASER_MOD_ERR
LASER_MOD_ERR.description:
The LASER_MOD_ERR is an alarm indicating mismatch of optical modules. When the optical module 
inserted does not support the service currently configured, this alarm occurs.
LASER_MOD_ERR.impact:
When the installed optical module is incorrect, the performance of the optical port is degraded. In severe 
cases, the services are interrupted.
possible_causes: The optical interface is configured as single mode, but a multi-mode optical module is used; or the optical interface is configured as multi-mode, but a single-mode optical module is used. ===== PAGE 237 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 235
The rate of the optical module inserted does not match the rate of the optical interface of the board.
The optical module is faulty.

LASER_MODULE_MISMATCH.name: LASER_MODULE_MISMATCH
LASER_MODULE_MISMATCH.description:
Optical modules mismatch. This alarm is generated when the type of the optical module inserted into an 
optical port of a board mismatches the type of the board.
LASER_MODULE_MISMATCH.impact: Services cannot be normally received or transmitted, and even may be interrupted.
possible_causes: The optical port type supported by the physical board mismatches the type of the optical module inserted to the optical port. • The logical port is inconsistent with the physical port.
The configuration of the logical port is inconsistent with the actual physical port where the optical module is installed. • The function configuration does not match the module.
After ST2 mode is enabled for the board, the BIDI OSC module is inserted.
The type of the OTDR module in the Alps-WDM scenario does not meet the requirement. • Parameter 1 is 0x01:
The use of optical ports on the optical module does not comply with the configuration principle. • Parameter 1 is 0x02:
The optical port does not support IEEE 1588 service configuration in the current networking. • Parameter 1 is 0x03:
After jitter detection is enabled, the inserted optical module is not supported.

LINK_ERR.name: LINK_ERR
LINK_ERR.description: Incorrect data link. This alarm is generated when the link status of Ethernet data ports is down.
LINK_ERR.impact:
When the link status of Ethernet ports is down, a valid link cannot be created between the two data ports 
and the data services are interrupted.

The input optical power of the two interconnected Ethernet ports is excessively high or low. ===== PAGE 241 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 239

The data equipment on the client side is faulty.
The board that reports this alarm is faulty.

LOCAL_FAULT.name: LOCAL_FAULT
LOCAL_FAULT.description: This alarm is generated when a local fault occurs.
LOCAL_FAULT.impact: If the board receives the LOCAL_FAULT alarm, the received services may be interrupted.
possible_causes: The input fiber on the client side is transiently cut.
The input optical power on the client side is abnormal.
The optical port of the optical module is contaminated.
The optical module is not properly connected.
The board software is abnormal.

LPT_ACTIVE.name: LPT_ACTIVE
LPT_ACTIVE.description:
This alarm indicates that LPT switching occurred. The data equipment itself has protection schemes. Hence, 
the protection provided by the WDM equipment is not needed. However, the WDM equipment is needed 
for informing the data equipment about the faults in the transmission layer. In this way, the switching 
would be triggered for the data equipment. The alarm is generated when switching is triggered.
LPT_ACTIVE.impact:
When this alarm is generated, services will be interrupted if no alternative route is available. If an 
alternative route is available, the services will be automatically switched to the available route, and a 
message will be generated, prompting the user to remove the fault.

LSR_WILL_DIE.name: LSR_WILL_DIE
LSR_WILL_DIE.description: This alarm indicates that the laser life will end.
LSR_WILL_DIE.impact:
The laser is aging, and therefore the quality of the output optical signals and the received signals is 
decreased (for example, the optical power is lower or is unstable). The impact depends on the aging level 
of the laser.
possible_causes: The laser is aging. The service life of the laser will be terminated.
The detection circuit of the board is faulty.

MEM_OVER.name: MEM_OVER
MEM_OVER.description:
The MEM_OVER alarm indicates that the memory utilization is too high. This alarm occurs when a board 
detects that the memory utilization is higher than the threshold.
MEM_OVER.impact: When this alarm occurs, the board might perform an automatic warm reset.
possible_causes: The NE is operating a large number of alarm and performance monitoring tasks.
The board is operating a large volume of traffic.

MOD_COM_FAIL.name: MOD_COM_FAIL
MOD_COM_FAIL.description:
Module communication abnormality. The alarm is generated when the communication between the CPU 
and other internal modules of the board is abnormal.
MOD_COM_FAIL.impact:
Because the communication between the CPU and the optical module is abnormal, the optical module 
cannot be managed by NCE and the information about the optical module cannot be queried.
possible_causes: The board is in poor contact with the connector of the optical module.
The software processing of the optical module on the board is faulty.
The board or optical module is faulty.

MS_AIS.name: MS_AIS
MS_AIS.description:
This alarm is a multiplex section alarm indication. The alarm is generated when the input signals from the 
client side contain the MS_AIS signal or the receive side of the local station is faulty.
possible_causes: The input signals from the client side contain the MS_AIS signal, as shown in the following figure. ===== PAGE 252 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 250
The board that reports the alarm is faulty.

opposite station back transmits the information through overhead when the WDM-side receive part of the 
opposite station is faulty (for example, the R_LOS, R_LOF or MS_AIS alarm is generated).

2026-04-22 251

MUT_LOS.name: MUT_LOS
MUT_LOS.description:
Multiplexed signals are lost. This alarm is generated when the multiplexed optical signals received by a 
board are lost.
MUT_LOS.impact: The services carried on the optical port where this alarm is generated are interrupted.
possible_causes: No fiber is connected to the optical port at the receive end of the board that reports the alarm, or the fiber is incorrectly connected or damaged.
The signal loss is too large during transmission.
The board that reports the alarm is faulty.

NEBD_XC_DIF.name: NEBD_XC_DIF
NEBD_XC_DIF.description:
The NE and board have inconsistent cross-connect data. For a board that supports service cross-
connections, this alarm is reported when the cross-connect data stored on the system control board is 
inconsistent with the cross-connect data stored on the board.
NEBD_XC_DIF.impact:
• New services may fail to be provisioned.
• The created services are abnormal. For the boards (cross-connect boards and system control boards) 
that have device-level protection, isolation or switching may be triggered. For service boards, services 
may be interrupted, or the protection switching function may be abnormal.
possible_causes: The cross-connect data stored on the board is incorrect. ===== PAGE 259 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 257
The cross-connect data stored on the system control board is incorrect.
The cross-connect board is faulty.

NO_ELABEL.name: NO_ELABEL
NO_ELABEL.description:
===== PAGE 260 =====
Electronic label unloaded. This alarm is generated when the electronic label of a board is lost or not 
loaded.
NO_ELABEL.impact:
• The logical versions of some service boards will change after a device upgrade. If no cold reset is 
performed on such a board, the logical version of the board is still the source version after the 
upgrade is completed.
• After the software is upgraded, the new version enhances the frequency deviation tolerance of the 
system clock. If no cold reset is performed, services may be transiently in
possible_causes: The electronic label is lost or not loaded.
The new board logic does not take effect.
After the software is upgraded, no cold reset is performed on the board, and the clock configuration of the earlier version does not take effect.
The board software communication is abnormal.

OA_LOW_GAIN.name: OA_LOW_GAIN
OA_LOW_GAIN.description:
Gain of an optical amplifier (OA) board being low. This alarm is generated when the actual gain of an OA 
board (except the Raman optical module of the RAU board) is 3 dB lower than the nominal gain. For the 
Raman optical module of the RAU board, the alarm is generated when the actual gain is 2 dB lower than 
the nominal gain.
OA_LOW_GAIN.impact:
The impacts of this alarm vary according to the alarm causes:
• If the alarm is generated because the input optical power is excessively high, the redundancy of the 
system decreases, which affects the subsequent capacity expansion.
===== PAGE 263 =====
• If the alarm is caused by other factors (for example, excessive insertion loss between the TDC and 
RDC optical ports on an OAU board), the inpu

ODU_SNCP_PS.name: ODU_SNCP_PS
ODU_SNCP_PS.description:
ODUk SNCP protection switching. This alarm is generated on the board of working channel when an ODU 
SNCP protection group actuates switching in which the current channel switches to the protection channel 
from the working channel.
ODU_SNCP_PS.impact:
When an ODUk SNCP protection group undergoes switching, services are transiently interrupted. When 
this alarm is reported, the working channel of the ODUk SNCP protection group might have faulty services 
that need to be restored.
ODU_SNCP_PS.fault_symptom:
Table 1 lists the fault symptoms for the ODU_SNCP_PS alarm. 
Table 1 Fault symptoms for the ODU_SNCP_PS alarm 
Fault Symptom Cause

as forced switching or manual switching.
Protection switching is performed, and the 
board on the working chann
possible_causes: A user delivers an external switching command such as forced switching or manual switching. Such a command switches the services of the ODUk SNCP protection group from the working channel to the protection channel.
The services on the working channel of the ODUk SNCP protection group are faulty and therefore services are automatically switched to the protection channel.

ODU_SNCP_WEAK.name: ODU_SNCP_WEAK
ODU_SNCP_WEAK.description:
ODUk SNCP weak protection capability. This alarm is generated on the board of working channel when 
the working and protection channels of a protection group are configured on the same OTU board. When 
the working and protection channels of a protection group are configured on different OTU boards and the 
working or protection channel on the sink NE of the SNCP protection group is faulty, this alarm is reported. 
Inverse multiplexing SNCP protection groups are not correctly added to the SNCP protection group set.
ODU_SNCP_WEAK.impact:
• The protection capability is weak.
• If the channel is faulty and ODUk SNCP switching occurs, services will be transiently interrupted.
• If inverse multiplexing SNCP protection groups are not correctly added to the SNCP protection group 
set, services will be affected when protection switching occurs on any ODUk SNCP protection group.
possible_causes: The working and protection channels of a protection group are configured on the same OTU board.
A service fault occurs in the working or protection channel of the ODUk SNCP protection group.
The working or protection OTU boards or cross-connect boards of the SNCP are faulty. ===== PAGE 269 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 267
Inverse multiplexing SNCP protection groups are not correctly added to the SNCP protection group set.

ODUk_LOFLOM.name: ODUk_LOFLOM
ODUk_LOFLOM.description:
Frame alignment signal (FAS) and multiframe alignment signal (MFAS) being abnormal. This alarm is 
generated when the upstream frame header does not match the downstream frame header.
k indicates the rate level, its value is FLEX, 0, 1, 2, 3, or 25.

possible_causes: The signals transmitted by the corresponding board at the opposite end do not have a frame structure.
The input optical power is abnormal.
The FEC type is incorrectly configured.
Bit errors in the received signals of the OTU board at the local station are excessive.
The fiber of the transmission line is abnormal.
The rate modes of corresponding channels on the local and opposite boards are inconsistent.
The ODUk timeslot configuration modes of the board at both ends are different.
The service mapping paths of the local and peer boards are inconsistent.
The local or opposite board is faulty.

ODUk_PM_EXC.name: ODUk_PM_EXC
ODUk_PM_EXC.description:
ODUk PM BIP8 error count exceeding the threshold. This alarm is generated when the BIP8 detection is in 
poisson mode and bit error count exceeds the threshold.
===== PAGE 272 =====
k indicates the level of rate. Its value is 3.
ODUk_PM_EXC.impact:
If this alarm is reported, bit errors will be generated on the services of this optical port, resulting service 
signal failure or service signal unavailability.

and the fiber transmission line is abnormal.

possible_causes: The attenuation of the received signals is rather large, and the fiber transmission line is abnormal.
The transmitter of the OTU board at the opposite station is faulty.
The receiver of the OTU board at local station is faulty.

OPA_FAIL_INDI.name: OPA_FAIL_INDI
OPA_FAIL_INDI.description:
===== PAGE 274 =====
Failure in automatic power adjustment of optical cross-connections. The alarm is generated when the 
calculated attenuation exceeds the adjustment range of the board during an automatic optical power 
adjustment.
OPA_FAIL_INDI.impact:
• When the alarm is reported, the attenuation of the board is not adjusted. For new services, the 
services may be unavailable. For existing services, the QoS cannot be improved.
• This alarm indicates an operation failure instead of a fault being detected. In other words, this alarm 
persists even after you manually adjust the attenuation and services are restored.
possible_causes: The optical power budget is insufficient.
The attenuation of the configured VA1 or VA4 board is manually modified.

When there are adjustment points of multiplexed wavelengths and each single wavelength in OPA scenarios, the attenuation of the VOAs at the multiplexed wavelength adjustment points is not adjusted to the minimum value. OTUk_LOF.description:
The OTUk_LOF is an alarm indicating that the frame alignment signal (FAS) is abnormal. This alarm occurs 
when the frame alignment processing is out of frame (OOF) in three consecutive milliseconds.
k indicates the level of rate. Its value is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 25.
OTUk_LOF.impact: Services on the board are interrupted.

OUT_PWR_HIGH.name: OUT_PWR_HIGH
OUT_PWR_HIGH.description:
Output optical power being too high. This alarm is generated when the laser output optical power exceeds 
the upper threshold.
===== PAGE 280 =====
2026-04-22 278
OUT_PWR_HIGH.impact:
• When the output optical power is excessively high, the input optical power at the receive end will be 
very high if no proper optical attenuator is used at the receive end. As a result, the module at the 
receive end may be damaged.
• If the board works abnormally, the existing services are affected.

PORT_MODULE_OFFLINE.name: PORT_MODULE_OFFLINE
PORT_MODULE_OFFLINE.description:
===== PAGE 281 =====
Optical module on an optical port being offline. This alarm is generated when the board detects that an 
optical module is offline.
PORT_MODULE_OFFLINE.impact: Absence of the optical module leads to an interruption of services carried at the corresponding optical port.
possible_causes: The optical module does not exist or is not correctly inserted.
The optical module or the board is faulty.

POWER_DIFF_OVER.name: POWER_DIFF_OVER
POWER_DIFF_OVER.description:
POWER_DIFF_OVER indicates that the optical power difference change exceeds the specified threshold. If 
the variance of the current power difference between active and standby optical signals from the initial 
power difference between active and standby optical signals exceeds the specified threshold, this alarm will 
be reported on the channel with lower power.
POWER_DIFF_OVER.impact:
The switching of the active and standby channels is affected. As a result, the quality of the received 
services is affected.
possible_causes: During transmission, the optical power attenuation of signals is excessively large or the board at the local end is equipped with an over-large optical attenuator. Therefore, the optical power difference between the active and standby OSCs at the receive end is excessively large. ===== PAGE 283 ====
The optical power difference of signals on the active and standby channels when the board at the peer end transmits signals is excessively large.
The detection circuit of the board at the local end is faulty.

POWER_FAIL.name: POWER_FAIL
POWER_FAIL.description:
Power supply failure. This alarm is generated when the power supply of a board becomes abnormal. For 
example, there is overvoltage or undervoltage of the power supply, or the battery on the system control 
board has no charge.
POWER_FAIL.impact:
• If this alarm is reported by the system control board (parameter 1 of this alarm is 0x05), the 
configuration within 30 minutes before the power failure may be lost. In this case, you need to 
manually redeliver the configuration data within 30 minutes before the power failure.
• If this alarm is reported by other boards, 
• If the active power supply fails but the standby power supply is normal
possible_causes: If the alarm is reported by the system control board (parameter 1 is 0x05), the battery power supply of the system control board is abnormal.
If the alarm is reported by the PIU board, the input power voltage of the subrack is abnormal and the power supply module is faulty (parameter 1 is 0x3d or 0x3f).

If the alarm is reported by the PIU board, the power supply module of the board is faulty or aging, the board is not properly installed, or the PIU board is set to the shutdown mode in the system control board configuration window (parameter 1 is not 0x05, 0x3d, or 0x3f).
If the PSU board reports this alarm, the input power of the subrack is abnormal and the power module is faulty. ===== PAGE 286 ===== OptiX OSN 9800 Product Documentation 2026-04-22 284

PUMP_COOL_EXC.name: PUMP_COOL_EXC
PUMP_COOL_EXC.description:
Cooling current of the pump laser exceeding the threshold. This alarm is generated when the laser cooling 
current is higher than the upper threshold or lower than the lower threshold.
PUMP_COOL_EXC.impact:
When this alarm is reported, the laser ages sharply and the performance of output signals deteriorates.
===== PAGE 288 =====
2026-04-22 286

Loss of frames on the receiving line. This alarm is generated when the frame alignment processing is out 
of frame (OOF) in 3 consecutive milliseconds.
R_LOF.impact:

• After this alarm is detected, protection switching is performed if the board supports protection 
switching.

R_LOS.name: R_LOS
R_LOS.description: Loss of signals at the receive end. This alarm is generated when the receive end receives no signal.
R_LOS.impact: Services carried at the optical port where this alarm is generated are interrupted.
possible_causes: (reported from the client side): No fiber jumper is connected to the optical port on the board of the local station, the fiber jumper connected to the optical port is loose, or the fiber jumper is connected incorrectly.
(reported from the client side): The line attenuation is excessively high or a fiber cut occurs.
(reported from the client side): The board that reports this alarm is faulty.
(reported from the client side): If the board reporting this alarm is a 40G or 100G board, at least one wavelength has been missing from the receive end of the board.

(reported from the WDM side): The laser of the board at the opposite station is shut down.
(reported from the WDM side): The transmit module of the opposite station or receive module of the local station is faulty.
(reported from the WDM side): For the coherent board, the actually received wavelength is inconsistent with the configured received wavelength on the board.

R_SLIP.description:
Frame slipping on the receive side. The alarm is generated when the phase deviation occurs in the received 
service frames of the OSC board.

This alarm affects the services carried by the OSC board. For example, the optical supervisory signals or 
clock signals are degraded. As a result, the NE is disconnected from the NCE system.

SECU_ALM.name: SECU_ALM
SECU_ALM.description:
Invalid access. This alarm is generated when a user fails to log in again after four consecutive login 
failures.
SECU_ALM.impact: The alarm automatically clears and has no impact on the system.

SUBRACK_ID_CONFLICT.name: SUBRACK_ID_CONFLICT
SUBRACK_ID_CONFLICT.description: This alarm is generated when a subrack ID conflict occurs in master-slave subrack mode.
SUBRACK_ID_CONFLICT.impact:
The inter-subrack communication is abnormal. As a result, commands cannot be correctly issued to 
corresponding subracks, and boards become unreachable by the NMS.
SUBRACK_ID_CONFLICT.fault_symptom:
The board may report a BD_STATUS, COMMUN_FAIL, or WRG_BD_TYPE alarm at the same time.
 
If no corresponding fault symptom occurs, or the fault symptom is not included in this section, handle the alarm by 
referring to the procedure below.

SUM_INPWR_LOW.name: SUM_INPWR_LOW
SUM_INPWR_LOW.description:
Input optical power of multiplexed wavelengths is excessively low. This alarm is generated when the input 
optical power of multiplexed signals is lower than the threshold.
SUM_INPWR_LOW.impact:
The output optical signals of a single channel of the board may be lost. As a result, the services in use may 
have bit errors or even are interrupted.
SUM_INPWR_LOW.fault_symptom:
Table 1 lists the fault symptom for the SUM_INPWR_LOW alarm. 
Table 1 Fault symptom for the SUM_INPWR_LOW alarm 
Fault Symptom Cause
The upstream board reports an 
OUT_PWR_LOW alarm.
Cause 1: The output optical power of the upstream station decreases. 
Therefore, the input optical power of the local station is excessively low.
 
If the fault has no symptom, or if the fault symptom is not covered i
possible_causes: The output optical power of the upstream station decreases. Therefore, the input optical power of the local station is excessively low.
The line attenuation is excessively high, or related fiber jumpers, fiber connectors, or optical attenuators are dirty.
The board that reports this alarm is faulty.

SWDL_CHGMNG_NOMATCH.name: SWDL_CHGMNG_NOMATCH
SWDL_CHGMNG_NOMATCH.description:
Software mismatching alarm after system control board replacement. The system re-checks whether the 
software of each board matches the NE software after the NE starts up upon a power failure or the system 
control board is replaced or reset (cold). This alarm is generated when the board software of a board 
mismatches the NE software.
SWDL_CHGMNG_NOMATCH.impact:
• When this alarm occurs, the automatic matching function for package loading is disabled.
• The version of the NE software is inconsistent with that of the system control board. Certain functions 
of the NE may operate abnormally.

SWDL_NEPKGCHECK.name: SWDL_NEPKGCHECK
SWDL_NEPKGCHECK.description:
Loss of files. This alarm is generated when the NE software checks the software package and finds that a 
file in a partition of the system control board software package is lost and the file cannot be restored from 
the related file in another partition. This alarm clears when the NE software checks the software package 
and finds the file during next preventive maintenance. 
 
The system control board checks the software package each time when the system control board starts up and when 
the periodical check is performed. The periodical check is performed every hour by default.
SWDL_NEPKGCHECK.impact:
• If the alarm is reported during package loading, the package loading will fail.
• If the alarm is reported at other time, the automatic matching function will be unavailable.

SYNC_C_LOS.name: SYNC_C_LOS
SYNC_C_LOS.description:
===== PAGE 310 =====
• In cluster and non-cluster scenarios, this alarm indicates that the level of the synchronization source 
from the service board or bidirectional OSC board is lost. That is, this alarm is generated when the 
clock source on the service board or bidirectional OSC board in the priority table is lost.
• In cluster scenarios, this alarm indicates that the time-scale source of the internal service subrack is 
lost, or the time-scale source of the standby CLC is lost.

• In cluster and non-cluster scenarios, this alarm is generated when the clock source is lost, indicating 
that the external clock source of the system is lost and the device cannot trace the external clock 
source.
• In cluster scenarios, this alarm is generated when the time-scale source is lost, indicating that the 
time-scale source is unavailable. Each service subrack has
possible_causes: Input signals are lost at the optical or electrical port that is connected to the clock source.
A fiber fault occurs.

The clock board is faulty. In a cluster scenario where the time-scale source is lost:
The clock fiber connection in the cluster is interrupted.
The optical module is faulty.
The system control board or clock distribution board is faulty.

TEMP_OVER.name: TEMP_OVER
TEMP_OVER.description:
Working temperature crossing the threshold. This alarm is generated when the system detects that the 
board working temperature is higher than the upper threshold or lower than the lower threshold.
TEMP_OVER.impact:
The excessively high or low temperature puts the system in a highly dangerous state. If the system runs in 
this state for a long period of time, bit errors may be generated and services may be interrupted. 
Therefore, the TEMP_OVER alarm must be handled in a timely manner.
possible_causes: The set rotating speed of the fan board is excessively low.
The fan board is faulty.
The air filter is excessively dusty.
The ambient temperature is excessively high or excessively low due to a cooler or heater equipment fault.
The fan is not in position.
The board that reports the alarm is faulty.
If the alarm is reported on the cross-board, the operation may be irregular. The vents on the cross-board are obstructed, causing the temperature of the board to be too high.

TF.name: TF
TF.description:
Transmission failure. This alarm is generated when the transmit optical power of the laser exceeds the 
threshold of the output optical power of the laser.
TF.impact:
If a laser transmission failure occurs, services are interrupted.
===== PAGE 316 =====
2026-04-22 314
possible_causes: The laser module is damaged, or the laser is aging.
The detection circuit of the board is faulty.

WRG_BD_TYPE.name: WRG_BD_TYPE
WRG_BD_TYPE.description:
Incorrect board type. This alarm is generated when the configured logical board type is inconsistent with 
the actual physical board type. This alarm is generated when the configured logical board is not supported 
by the current device.
WRG_BD_TYPE.impact:
If the type of the logical board is different from the type of the physical board, the board cannot work 
properly, affecting services.
possible_causes: The type of the logical board configured on the NCE is different from the type of the physical board installed in the slot.
The board that reports this alarm is faulty.
The logical board supported by the patch version is added. After the patch is uninstalled, the current software version does not support the logical board.
